title: Per-layer FlashAttention adapter, quantile-driven tuning and decode stability plan
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: We observe intermittent latency and correctness regressions when routing between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernel implementations for long-sequence decode workloads. This task implements a per-layer, quantile-driven adapter that chooses the most stable kernel variant per-layer at runtime, plus a lightweight sentinel that detects early signs of decode instability and triggers safe fallback behavior.

Background: Recent canaries showed that some long-context chat generation traces produce higher tail latency and occasional token misordering after switching to the v3 path on certain layer shapes and quantized weights. Existing global kernel selectors pick a single variant for the whole model which misses per-layer heterogeneity (e.g., some layers are bandwidth-bound, some are compute-bound). We need a low-risk mitigation that preserves v3 gains while preventing regressions.

What we're building: 1) A layer-adaptive selection module that samples runtime Q/K/V statistics and uses quantile estimates of per-layer latency and memory to pick v2/v3/hybrid for each layer. 2) A micro-prober that runs a small number of synthetic decode fragments (fast, off the hot path) to validate chosen configuration at startup and after hot reloads. 3) A decode-stability sentinel that watches token timing and KV-cache metrics to detect divergence or jitter and triggers a graceful rollback to a previously known-good layer map.

Scope: Implement selection logic in serving runtime, add light-weight telemetry hooks, extend canary harness for per-layer probes, add config/console toggle to force global vs per-layer behavior, and create an automated rollback policy for customer routes.

Risks and trade-offs: - Per-layer decisions increase decision overhead at startup; we limit runtime cost by caching maps and only re-evaluating on model/version changes. - Probing adds a small startup latency; probes are async and time-bounded to avoid impacting SLOs. - Quantile estimation requires telemetry; we'll use streaming sketches to keep memory use low.

Artifacts: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Per-layer+FlashAttention+Adapter; Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1247; Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/attn/per-layer-canary?orgId=1
acceptance_criteria: Per-layer selector implemented and enabled behind feature flag
Micro-prober runs within configured timeout and logs probe outcomes
Decode-stability sentinel detects divergence within configured thresholds and triggers fallback
Canary job showing no increase in token error rate or >95th latency for two weeks on standard traces
Documentation updated (Confluence + release notes) and runtime-1.19 release contains migration steps
tasks: Design and add quantile sketch telemetry for per-layer latency and memory usage
Implement selector algorithm (quantile thresholds + hysteresis) inside kernel router
Build micro-prober harness: synthetic short-fragment decode run with KV-cache replay
Add sentinel: token-timing jitter detector and divergence heuristic
Integration tests: model fixtures (LLaMA-like long-context, chat RLHF traces)
Canary rollout plan and dashboard panels
Documentation: console toggle, config params, troubleshooting guide
notes: 2025-02-20: Spike complete — naive per-layer baseline improves tail-latency in microbenchmarks but introduced two rare mis-order tokens in decode harness.
2025-02-24: Decided to prefer a conservative hysteresis (3 sample confirmations) before switching a layer variant to reduce oscillation.
2025-02-26: Security review not required for telemetry changes (sketches are aggregate and do not contain PII).
2025-02-28: Marcus validated micro-prober on a dedicated GPU instance; sample probe time ~120ms capped via timeout config.

telemetry_queries: high_tail_latency_by_layer: SELECT percentile_95(latency_ms) BY layer FROM attn_kernel_telemetry WHERE job='canary'
kv_cache_fragmentation: SELECT avg(fragmentation_ratio) BY shard FROM kv_cache_stats WHERE model=~'llama.*'
sentinel_triggers: SELECT count() FROM decode_sentinel_events WHERE reason!='none' AND timestamp >= now() - 7d
rollout_plan: lab canary: enable per-layer selector for internal test routes only (1 week)
staged canary: enable on 1% of customer traffic with real workloads for 2 weeks
automated rollback: if sentinel_triggers > 0.1% or p95 latency increases by >10% revert config for affected route
full rollout: increase to 100% after 2 weeks of stable metrics or PM sign-off
mitigations: Fallback to global v2 path if micro-prober fails three consecutive times
Reduce probe frequency and increase timeout in constrained environments
Add canary-specific logging for any token divergence to aid root cause analysis
Provide console toggle for immediate forced-global-decision per-route (ops-only)
